All four Web framework runs passed the Prompt menu/focus case. All four W3C runs passed Prompt typing, model Escape, keyboard copy/clear/paste, five real window widths, submission, and CodeBlock/StreamingText clipboard operations. Firefox additionally completed every readonly check.

Chrome's readonly failure is the empty selected substring at source line 228, after the line-227 document-text-unchanged assertion had passed. It is not document deletion, and Cut was not issued. Edge/Safari had received ArrowRight but did not meet the readonly-caret condition; Paste was not issued. Diagnostic `draft`/`focused` fields in this version still describe Prompt and cannot stand in for document state.

The remaining framework composition failures occur while checking an injected value before the corresponding Enter/resize action. They do not show that those actions broke real OS IME composition. The later stock-control experiment remains a separate evidence record. No assertion, platform status or full assistive-technology acceptance is promoted by this summary.
